title: Genome-Based Elucidation of Taxonomy, Pan-Genome Features and Secondary Metabolic Synthetic Capacity of Streptomyces griseorubens Strain MEPSL1 Isolated from Sweet Potato Roots
content: Streptomyces griseorubens strain MEPSL1 is an endophytic actinomycetes isolated from sweet potato roots, with its 16S rRNA gene and genome sequence previously deposited in the NCBI database. To clarify both its taxonomic position and its strain-level biological significance, phylogenomic, comparative genomic and functional genome-mining analyses were performed. Using the Type Strain Genome Server (TYGS), digital DNA–DNA hybridization (dDDH) and phylogenetic analysis were performed to clarify its taxonomic status. The dDDH results showed that the d0 values between MEPSL1 and the type strains S. griseorubens JCM 4383 and DSM 40160 were 81.2% and 81.9%, respectively, both above the 70% prokaryotic species threshold, with G + C content differences below 1% and d4 similarity up to 91.6%, confirming MEPSL1 as Streptomyces griseorubens. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) analysis among 20 Streptomyces strains verified its generic affiliation. Pan-genome analysis revealed a typical open pan-genome with 19,872 pan-genes and 3056 core genes. COG annotation showed that metabolism-related genes were the most abundant, supporting its environmental adaptability and secondary metabolite biosynthesis potential. AntiSMASH predicted 24 secondary metabolite biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), including four 100% identical to known clusters and seven putative novel clusters. Compared with previously reported S. griseorubens genomes from type collections, soil and animal-associated sources, MEPSL1 provides new genomic information for a sweet-potato-root endophytic lineage, including a desferrioxamine-like siderophore cluster, an ectoine stress-protection cluster, and predicted genes associated with nutrient adaptation, biofilm formation and host colonization. Antimicrobial resistance gene analysis detected multiple resistance determinants against macrolides, tetracyclines, β-lactams, and other classes. Virulence factor profiling identified genes related to nutritional adaptation, immune modulation, and biofilm formation. This study provides genomic insights into the taxonomy, adaptability, metabolic potential, resistance, and virulence features of MEPSL1, thereby supporting future applications in natural product discovery and plant-associated microbial resource development.
